If you look at the incoming tab it looks like we're getting about 100 submissions an hour. I think the big issue is something I've mentioned repeatedly. This soft of software is not actually good for discussion on a large scale. Most people only look at the most popular topics which in turn leads to them getting more upvotes making the front and other popularity based metrics become stagnant (since they receive ever more upvotes making it ever more difficult for other content to replace them) even when there is a time based deterioration metric in play.

You can see a microcosm of the same effect even on the comments when articles end up getting a lot. Everything except the top few comments end up getting completely buried. And as most people don't tend to scroll far down before moving onto the next topic they stay buried while the comments at the top get more and more upvoted.

Things need to be rethought. For instance one idea would be to have a couple of prominent slots in comments/submissions reserved for wildcards. These would be prominently displayed randomly chosen comments/submissions that are not upvoted (or downvoted) much to simply give people exposure to fresh content and also give said content a chance to rise to the top without relying just on the people that do voluntarily go dig through the masses of new content. This is also the reason that voting manipulation and such is so effective on this software. Get just 10 people to start upvoting reasonably interest content and it's going to hit the frontpage and get put in the 'upvote cycle' whereas without those 10 booster points it would likely more often than not just end up getting passed through along with all of the other content nobody ever gets a chance to see.
